exposure.needed: whether the configured Cilium cluster name violates the 32-char lowercase alphanumeric/'-' rule

original.statement: Cilium cluster name is now validated (max 32 lowercase alphanumerics or '-', starting and ending alphanumeric); bypass via upgradeCompatibility v1.15 or earlier, strictly enforced from v1.17.

of.needed: the configured Cilium cluster name and whether it violates the at-most-32 lowercase alphanumeric/'-' rule (start/end alphanumeric); the evidence does not name the key carrying it

corrected.statement: In Cilium 1.16.0, an environment is exposed if its cluster name breaks the new rule (at most 32 lowercase alphanumeric characters or '-', starting and ending with an alphanumeric character) and upgradeCompatibility is not set to v1.15 or earlier. Environments with upgradeCompatibility at v1.15 or earlier bypass the check for now; it is strictly enforced from v1.17.

decision.reason: [ev-6e35b4906b1d] says cluster names are now checked against the 32-char lowercase alphanumeric/'-' rule. It does not name the configuration key that holds the cluster name or give its default, so whether a name breaks the rule stays undecidable. The same evidence says the check is bypassed only when `upgradeCompatibility` is v1.15 or earlier, so the proposed overlap (`upgradeCompatibility` set to any value) is too broad: a value of 1.16 does not protect anything. Exposure should also leave out environments that use the bypass.
